gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-006 concerns unjustified gradient consistency of a surrogate gap at a boundary. It does not identify the distinct false equality between the normalized feasible-direction residual and the gradient/normal-cone residual, nor the same-epsilon interior interpretation.

ISSUE-006 diagnoses a boundary error in inferring zero gradient from a constrained majorization gap. It does not diagnose the failed standalone stationary-point identity, including its negative feasible-direction supremum, zero normal-cone distance, and required truncation.

Both identify the false uniform supremum over unrestricted initializations: proof constants depend on the initial gap, and a quadratic example makes the worst-case hitting time infinite. Both give the bounded-initialization or initialization-dependent repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed worst-case complexity is not uniform over all initializations because the initial objective gap and related constants are unbounded; fixed-initialization rates may remain valid.

component_coverage.gold_component: Unrestricted initialization supremum makes the stated uniform complexity infinite or unsupported because proof constants depend on the initial gap.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly identifies the unrestricted initialization supremum, unbounded initial-gap constants, an infinite hitting-time example, affected corollaries, and the bounded-initialization repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the invalid inference that equality of a constrained majorizing surrogate and objective at the base point implies gradient equality at a boundary. Both recognize the resulting proof failure and require explicit gradient consistency.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Constrained-domain majorization and value equality do not imply tangency/gradient consistency at boundary base points, so the load-bearing gradient identities and downstream bounds are unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: Constrained-domain majorization plus value equality does not imply gradient tangency at a boundary, invalidating the key lemma and stationarity chain.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 gives the boundary counterexample, explains the directional-derivative distinction and downstream uncontrolled terms, and supplies the gradient-consistency repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the lower bound on the majorization gap does not imply strong convexity of the surrogate, while the proposition uses strong convexity under only A1-A4. Both provide a constant-surrogate counterexample and the A5(b) repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The asymptotic parameter-gap conclusion uses surrogate strong convexity that is absent from A1-A4; a quadratic gap condition alone does not supply it.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proposition falsely derives asymptotic exactness from A1-A4 while using strong convexity available only under A5(b).
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-008 explicitly distinguishes the gap lower bound from surrogate strong convexity, supplies a counterexample, identifies affected uses, and proposes adding A5(b).

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the NMF/nonnegative factor-domain scaling invariance that makes sublevel sets noncompact, invalidates A2 and the boundedness proposition, and leaves the application theorem unsupported. The prediction also gives compatible compact-domain or boundedness repairs.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The advertised unbounded NMF factor domain has noncompact sublevel sets due to scale invariance, so the claimed compactness/boundedness and resulting theorem application are unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: NMF factor scaling destroys compact sublevels and therefore the boundedness and smoothness prerequisites used for the corollary.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-013 explicitly gives the NMF scaling family, identifies failure of A2 and boundedness, traces the theorem/application consequence, and states compact-domain or new boundedness repairs.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-011 concerns stale versus updated blocks and algorithmic update order. It does not identify the missing cross-block terms in the displayed gradient-difference formula or the polynomial-Hessian replacement proof required by I027.

Both identify the incompatible centering of the surrogate: the proof/update uses the thresholded center while sharpness is stated at the unthresholded iterate. Both show the resulting wrong minimizer or loss of sharpness, theorem failure, and shifted-domain repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The surrogate cannot simultaneously be centered at the current iterate for sharpness and at the thresholded iterate for the printed update; this invalidates exact minimization/BMM identification and the original-domain guarantees.

component_coverage.gold_component: Thresholded versus unthresholded surrogate centering makes the printed update nonoptimal or destroys sharpness, invalidating the BMM application.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-012 explicitly analyzes both possible centers, gives the discrepancy and thresholding witness, traces the failed BMM conditions, and supplies the shifted-constraint repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the displayed ALS/CTF updates use stale blocks simultaneously, whereas the theorem requires cyclic use of newly updated preceding blocks. Both recognize that this breaks the BMM identification and can produce nonstationary behavior, with the cyclic-update repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The advertised tensor/block updates are Jacobi rather than the cyclic updates analyzed by BMM-DR, so the theorem's monotonicity and stationarity guarantees do not apply.

component_coverage.gold_component: Stale-block simultaneous updates are not the cyclic BMM-DR updates and can yield nonstationary cycles, invalidating the application.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-011 explicitly contrasts Jacobi and cyclic block order, identifies affected BMM applications, and gives the updated-block repair.
